rows.description: A friend notices your exhaustion and says you should rest. Accept the concern instead of joking it away. Small acts like a walk or shared meal help, and letting people care for you is part of recovery.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, guilt, indifference, neglect, resentment, trust
related mind states: tiredness, empathy
possibly related concept (heuristic): Empathic distress vs compassion

rows.description: You finally seek help for exhaustion and low mood. Being honest about symptoms and habits allows better care. Seeking help is strength, and many young professionals in India are learning that it is normal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, guilt, indifference, neglect, resentment
related mind states: tiredness, trust

rows.description: The dream career feels empty after the novelty ends. Ask what parts of the work still matter, what you are avoiding, and what you want. Sometimes the change is a role, a team, a rhythm, rather than everything.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, guilt, indifference, neglect, resentment, trust

rows.description: A friend dies young, and it shakes your sense of safety. Let grief be messy: attend the rites, share stories, cry, and check on their family. Numbing with work or alcohol only delays it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, comfort, compassion, guilt, indifference, protectiveness
related mind states: sadness, grief, detachment, trust

rows.description: You feel guilty for having been far away or busy when they died. Guilt often shows love and helplessness. Speak it aloud to someone, write what you would have said, and honour them by how you live now.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, comfort, compassion, grief, indifference, protectiveness
related mind states: affection, guilt

rows.description: Grief sparks fights over rituals, property and blame among relatives. Remember everyone is hurting. Delay legal talk, get elders or a neutral mediator, and keep the dead person's memory from becoming a battlefield.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, compassion, grief, guilt, indifference, protectiveness
related mind states: grief, hurt

rows.description: Friends bring food and sit silently with you. Accept the help, even if you cannot speak. Their steady presence, not wise words, is comfort. Tell them what you need in the weeks after, since support fades quickly.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, comfort, grief, guilt, indifference, protectiveness
related mind states: empathy

rows.description: Rituals, prayers and scripture hold you when reason cannot. Take comfort without demanding that pain vanish. If faith feels shaken, that too is part of mourning and can be spoken to a trusted person.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, compassion, grief, guilt, indifference, protectiveness
related mind states: grief, trust, hurt

rows.description: You feel nothing and worry something is wrong with you. Numbness is a common early response. Keep basic routines, let feelings come when they will, and seek counselling if it stays heavy for a long time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, comfort, compassion, grief, guilt, indifference
related mind states: anxiety, detachment

rows.description: A workplace expects quick return and speaks little of your loss. It hurts to feel invisible. Use leave, tell one trusted colleague, and set limits. Ask your manager for reduced load rather than forcing normal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, comfort, compassion, grief, guilt, protectiveness
related mind states: trust, hurt
